gaps: Federal, statewide, State Assembly and judicial-retention candidates are NOT on the ROV "Local Candidate Roster" (local contests only). They were taken from the county's official sample ballots inside the County Voter Information Guide composite (ballot-style pages). Party preference is as printed there; no website/email/incumbent data exists for them in an official county list (all null). The SOS certified candidate list was not consulted.

The Local Candidate Roster is a snapshot printed 8/20/2026 (file candidate-roster-(35)). The later County VIG sample ballots agree with it on all 37 contested local contests (same candidates and designations; only line-wrap whitespace differs). No newer roster was found on the ROV page. The write-in roster is dated 10/6/2026 and may change before the Oct 20 write-in filing deadline.

No county offices (Board of Supervisors, Sheriff, District Attorney, Assessor, etc.) appear on the Nov 3 ballot: not in the Notice of Election, Offices Up For Election, or any of the 131 sample ballot styles. The Notice lists "Judge of the Superior Court - 7 seats (Subject to Elections Code 8203)" but no Superior Court contest appears on any sample ballot. No State Senate contest is on San Joaquin County ballots. No county-level runoffs exist.

75 roster contests are flagged "On Ballot: No" (candidates do not exceed seats; appointment in lieu of election). They are in appointed_in_lieu, not contests. 13 contests listed in the Notice of Election have no qualified candidate in the roster at all (see no_candidate_contests); outcome (appointment or vacancy) not published on the pages fetched.

Candidate Statements of Qualifications (pdf pp. 540-577 of the VIG composite) were not extracted; only page references (soq_vig_pdf_page) and the roster "statement filed" flags are recorded. Some statements mention campaign websites, but these are not from the official list and were not recorded.

Interactive lookup tools (Omniballot sample-ballot lookup, votinginfotool.org widget, ArcGIS maps, BallotTrax) were identified but not exercised; they need an address/voter identity. Instead a precinct-to-ballot-type crosswalk was derived from the ROV association list PDF (1,180 regular precincts -> 131 ballot types; see precinct_ballot_type.json and ballot_styles.json).
ROV FAQ page content loads dynamically and was not captured. The ROV home "Sample Ballot" quick link (/department/rov/voting/sample-ballot-options) returns HTTP 404.

Source conflicts: (a) drop boxes available "starting October 2" (ROV drop-box page) vs "October 5" (VIG, calendar); (b) ROV email registrar@sjgov.org (website) vs registration@sjgov.org and vbm@sjgov.org (VIG); (c) VIG table of contents page ranges are shifted relative to actual content (ballot styles pdf pp. 16-539, candidate statements pp. 540-577, measures pp. 578-596).

Voter's Choice Act status is inferred (San Joaquin absent from the SOS VCA county list; ROV materials describe assigned polling places and countywide "No Wrong Location" voting). The ROV pages fetched do not state VCA status explicitly. The SOS list page may not reflect counties that adopted VCA after 2022.

Measure G (Galt Joint Union High School District) is administered with Sacramento County as lead county; only the SJ portion of the district is on San Joaquin ballots (3 ballot types). Spanish and other-language documents (Spanish VIG, Notices, facsimile ballots) were not downloaded.

Incumbent flag is set only where the county list prints the ballot designation "Incumbent" or "Appointed Incumbent" (local contests). Statewide/federal/Assembly incumbency is not stated in the county list (null).

bio.en: Qualified candidate for Lammersville USD Trustee Area 5 and the only nominee, so the seat is not on the ballot. Not a current trustee: the district lists Area 5 as “to be determined from the 2026 election”, and under Education Code §5328 she is expected to be seated at the board’s organizational meeting on Dec 16, 2026. In a Sept 2026 Mountain House Matters interview and at its Sept 30 candidate forum she described herself as a Mountain House resident since about 2015 with five children, four in district schools; an art teacher for the County Office of Education at Mountain House schools and a former high-school foreign-language teacher; a five-year Wicklund School Foundation board member; and a three-year member of the district’s facilities subcommittee. She is not listed in the district’s staff directory and said she has no campaign website. No board action naming her had been posted as of Oct 8, 2026.
bio.es: Candidata calificada al Área 5 del LUSD y única nominada, por lo que el escaño no está en la boleta. No es miembro actual: el distrito indica que el Área 5 “se determinará en la elección de 2026”, y según el Código de Educación §5328 se espera que tome posesión en la reunión de organización de la junta el 16 de diciembre de 2026. En una entrevista de Mountain House Matters de septiembre de 2026 y en su foro de candidatos del 30 de septiembre se describió como residente de Mountain House desde alrededor de 2015 con cinco hijos, cuatro en escuelas del distrito; maestra de arte de la Oficina de Educación del Condado en escuelas de Mountain House y exmaestra de idiomas de preparatoria; integrante durante cinco años de la junta de la Wicklund School Foundation; y miembro durante tres años del subcomité de instalaciones del distrito. No figura en el directorio de personal del distrito y dijo no tener sitio web de campaña. Al 8 de octubre de 2026 no se había publicado ninguna acción de la junta con su nombre.

local_measures.question: To provide safe, modern schools by upgrading/repairing aging classrooms, science labs, career technology and school facilities to support college/career readiness in math, science, technology, arts, engineering, and skilled trades; and fixing deteriorating roofs, plumbing, HVAC, and electrical systems; shall Escalon Unified School District's measure authorizing $26,000,000 in bonds at legal rates be adopted, levying approximately $18 per $100,000 assessed value ($1,700,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with independent audits, citizen oversight and all money locally controlled?
